charter.contribution: Stated verbatim in proposal v0.2 §14 (and echoed in CLAUDE.md): "We construct a finite computational world in which physical state, Bayesian belief state, and future-observation distributions are exactly available, then vary telemetry, context, coupling, and model scale to measure what information the trace makes knowable, what a transformer makes accessible internally, and what its exported prediction makes visible." Two qualifications from the later documents. (1) Both literature notes (2026-08-11, re-checked 2026-09-18) say the novelty exists only as a conjunction: interface-as-variable over a fixed generator, times exact ceilings, times the three-gap decomposition, times a structured systems world. "A world with exact posterior ceilings" and "excess loss over Bayes" are each already published and cannot be claimed alone. (2) Under the committed cut, paper 1 claims only the first two of the three verbs (knowable, and accessible via the belief-geometry slice), plus interface and context manipulation. "Coupling" belongs to paper 2 and "what its exported prediction makes visible" (exposure/use) belongs to paper 3. Paper 1's sentence is therefore narrower than the proposal's: build the exact world, vary telemetry (interface ladder r0–r4 plus the D8 order mode) and context (truncation windows), measure the exact observation gap per condition, and compare a from-scratch small transformer's next-record predictions and linearly accessible belief against the exact ceilings (corpus-track ceilings, per Part II v0.2.9).

rqs.text: Observability: how do telemetry fields, context horizon, and synchronization markers change the exact posterior uncertainty over latent computational state?
rqs.source: proposal v0.2 §4; operationalized by Part I deliverable 4 and Part II §5-§6 (rung collapse δ, synchronization horizon δ_sync); Milestones 1 and 3
rqs.status_now: Largely answered on the exact side, for the telemetry and context parts only. (a) Full-context injectivity theorem: from reset, every posterior is a point mass at every content rung r1–r4, so the ladder separates only under truncation or the D8 shuffled channel. (b) Straight-line C1 (14,·,2) under frozen δ = 0.01: collapse horizons L* = 2 (r3→r4), 8 (r2→r3), 10 (r1→r2); synchronization L* = 12 for r1 and 10 for r2–r4. Held-out Tier-1 P1 PASS. (c) Exit law (40,8,2) on looping C1′, enacted 2026-09-13 (exit-clause note): every adjacent pair r1–r4 is above δ at both statutory ε on the canonical track. The corpus track (the observer the model actually is) has a larger ladder in H(q|Πw): 0.39/0.20/0.02 bits at ε = 1. (d) D8 order-mode contrast measured in C0b and C1. (e) Synchronization markers and snapshots are NOT measured: TIME_CLASS (the anchored condition) was UNBUILT as of the 2026-09-01 map, and no snapshot mechanism exists in Part II. The 'synchronization markers' leg of RQ1 is open.

rqs.text: Predictive representation: do small transformers converge toward the exact belief state, a lower-dimensional predictive state, or another representation? Which distinctions become linearly accessible, and at which layers?
rqs.source: proposal v0.2 §4, §8.2-8.3; in paper 1's cut only as 'the belief-geometry slice of Milestone 5' (CLAUDE.md cut)
rqs.status_now: In progress; see learner note. Commit messages record a coordinate-free belief-geometry design v0.1 (the exact next-kind belief P*(kind_{k+1}|prefix) at position p0, with representation KL beside output KL). Findings recorded there: OIR 1.000 at k=1 in all 15 runs; at k=4 a seed-resolved layer-1 ordering r1 > r2 > r3 > r4; accessibility falls with context. Entity identities are fetched by attention rather than held at the record boundary (probe v0.3). The proposal's full question (belief state vs. predictive state vs. implementation state, across layers) is not yet answered: the probed target is next-kind predictive belief, not the hidden-state posterior vector of §8.2.

rqs.text: Emergence and scale: how do data volume, model capacity, context length, and predictive-state complexity determine the threshold at which the model approaches the exact information ceiling?
rqs.source: proposal v0.2 §4. Only partly in paper 1's cut: M2 ('confirm small transformers approach the exact next-event predictor on the simplest interface') and M3 (context truncation) are in; 'map selected transitions over model size and data volume' is Milestone 4, which falls outside the stated cut.
rqs.status_now: Partially explored; see learner note. Commits record a 2M-window data-volume axis at r1/r4 ε = 1 and a width axis (d64/128/256) with a learning-rate sweep (note §22). §22.1 finds 'budget, not rate': at 15 epochs every width improves, but the size axis is non-monotone at matched budget (0.088/0.047/0.070 at d64/128/256, seed 1). Seeds 2–3 and a 45-epoch d256 run were queued 2026-09-28. Models are about 0.85M params, below the proposal's 1M–50M range. Context length enters only as the prefix position k inside a fixed L = 8 window. No threshold has been established.

rqs.text: Do small transformers approach the exact next-event predictor on the simplest interface? (Milestone 2 acceptance question)
rqs.source: proposal §11 Milestone 2; learner-model-vs-ceiling-contract v0.1 §2.1-2.2 (primary number = law-mass mean of the pattern-projected per-window KL excess at k = L−1, against the corpus-track ceiling)
rqs.status_now: Measured; see learner note. From commit messages: at ε = ½ with six seeds, mean excess is r0 0.005 < r1 0.089 ≈ r3 0.092 < r4 0.118 < r2 0.124 bits. That ordering is not seed-wise stable, and the model is not at the ceiling at the content rungs (the δ it would need to reach is 0.01). Note that r0 ('simplest interface') is nearly at ceiling.

rqs.id: RQ3 / RQ4 (out of cut, listed for completeness)
rqs.text: RQ3 factorization/coupling → paper 2. RQ4 internal vs exported information, causal use → paper 3.
rqs.status_now: Not in paper 1. However, learner-note sections §17–§19 (per commit messages) already make exposure-style measurements: 'the which-thread question is an exposure question, answered without a probe', representation KL beside output KL, and §19.5 marking patching as M5 causal-use. See drift.

hypotheses.text: Predictive-state alignment: at adequate data and capacity, activations align more closely with the exact belief or predictive state than with the complete implementation-level simulator state.
hypotheses.falsifier: The implied falsifier is that affine/linear alignment to the implementation-level state (the realized X_t, or the full state tuple) is as good as or better than alignment to the exact posterior or predictive vector, on held-out windows, with probe-capacity controls. Proposal §10 also names a negative result: failure to align with exact belief geometry despite sufficient predictive performance would challenge existing belief-state accounts.
hypotheses.source: proposal v0.2 §9 H1, §8.2; belief-geometry slice of M5 (in cut)
hypotheses.status_now: Not tested as stated; see learner note. The current probe targets the next-kind predictive belief and lock-owner posteriors. No recorded comparison against an implementation-state target was found in these files.

hypotheses.text: Uncertainty preservation: for histories compatible with multiple hidden states, the model represents posterior uncertainty rather than collapsing to a maximum-likelihood state; activation geometry tracks the exact posterior simplex.
hypotheses.falsifier: Probe-decoded beliefs on ambiguous windows would be near-one-hot on the argmax state, or calibration against the exact posterior would fail where the exact posterior is non-degenerate.
hypotheses.source: proposal v0.2 §9 H2 (belief-geometry slice, in cut)
hypotheses.status_now: Partial evidence; see learner note. Commit messages mention hedging on near-determined blockers (H̃ 0.19–0.30 vs H* 0.07 at BLOCK, §19.6), which is over-dispersion rather than collapse. The OIR 1.000 results at k=1 are a boundary value; the house rule requires rechecking them at the finest grain, and the files read here do not show whether that was done. Open.

hypotheses.text: Informative-interface response: adding causally informative telemetry reduces the exact observation gap and induces corresponding changes in learned geometry and probe performance. Entropy-matched irrelevant telemetry does not produce the same gain.
hypotheses.falsifier: Exact side: an adjacent rung that changes no Q1–Q5 posterior and no preregistered P-horizon test (Part I D2 redesign trigger), or a decoy field that changes any ceiling (Part II §9 witness 4, exact zero required). Learner side: learned gains equal between the informative field and the entropy-matched decoy (the decoy preserving P(field|EVENT_KIND) per the D2 refinement), or no learned change tracking the ceiling change.
hypotheses.source: proposal §9 H3, §6.1; Part I D2 (+ v0.2.2 control refinement); Part II §9 witnesses 1, 2, 4, 5, 11
hypotheses.status_now: Exact half: largely confirmed (witnesses 3, 5, 6, 7, 11 SATISFIED; witnesses 1 and 2 evidenced but not enumerated as witness tests; exit-law ladder separated). The control half is untestable: witness 4 (ctrl-irr decoy) is UNBUILT, with no decoy field in the schema, and Part II §4 names none. The learned half is mixed; see learner note. Learner excess is non-monotone in rung (r2 worst at ε = ½), and the belief-accessibility ordering is r1 > r2 > r3 > r4, the reverse of information content. Neither contradicts H3 directly, because excess is measured relative to each rung's own ceiling. The 'corresponding change in learned geometry' is not established.

hypotheses.text: Context as observability: removing causally relevant history increases posterior uncertainty and imposes an irreducible ceiling; explicit synchronization or snapshot information restores a predictable portion of the loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Exact posterior entropy not increasing under truncation, or snapshot/TIME_CLASS anchoring restoring none (or an unpredicted amount) of the lost information. Part I D1: the rungs collapsing to certainty under long context (over-synchronization).
hypotheses.source: proposal §9 H5, §6.2; Part I D1 falsifier; Part II §2 (a)–(e), §6 synchronization horizon
hypotheses.status_now: First clause confirmed exactly: the full-context injectivity theorem, truncation-only grip, and measured synchronization horizons. The D1 falsifier FIRED at full context by theorem (Part A); Part B gives collapse horizons along L. The PI decided no contingency, and the looping world C1′ was adopted instead. Second clause (restoration by synchronization or snapshot) is UNTESTED: TIME_CLASS/anchored condition unbuilt as of 2026-09-01 and no snapshot mechanism exists. Learner side: interior-prefix curve only (contract §2.2, exploratory); see learner note.

hypotheses.text: Scaling toward, not through, the ceiling: more data and capacity reduce the accessible-representation gap but cannot reduce interface-imposed uncertainty; scaling curves approach interface-specific ceilings.
hypotheses.falsifier: The model's loss going below the exact corpus-track ceiling for its interface (impossible by construction if the ceiling is right, so it would indicate a ceiling or naming-bridge error). Or scaling curves converging to one universal level across rungs rather than to rung-specific ceilings.
hypotheses.source: proposal §9 H7; the capacity/data mapping is Milestone 4 (outside the stated cut), while interface-specific ceilings are M3
hypotheses.status_now: Early; see learner note. Excess is measured against rung-specific corpus ceilings, so 'toward' is the right frame. The size axis is non-monotone at matched budget, and more epochs help every width, which suggests under-training. There are no multi-seed scaling curves yet (seeds 2–3 queued 2026-09-28).

hypotheses.text: Part I exit clause: M1 succeeds if rungs show measurably distinct observability regimes within tractable support bounds AND there exist history classes where immediate predictions agree but longer-horizon distributions differ.
hypotheses.falsifier: Rung collapse (over-synchronization), support explosion (D4 violation), or no immediate-agree/later-diverge class. Any of these forces a world redesign before GPU time.
hypotheses.source: yupana-m1-spec-draft.md 'Deliverables and exit criteria'; exit-clause-40-8-2-note-v0.1.md; looping-exit-law-freeze-v0.1.md
hypotheses.status_now: Met as read by the exit-clause note (enacted 2026-09-13). On looping C1′ at (40,8,2), every adjacent pair r1–r4 is above δ at both statutory ε, and the divergent classes are exhibited. 'Across rungs' is read as r1–r4, with r0 reported beside; that reading is the researcher's interpretive decision. Canonical track only. As of the 09-01 map, deliverables 1–3 remained PARTIAL: no machine-checkable spec artifact, TIME_CLASS absent, shuffled gates on C0b only, D7 check unbuilt, and witness executables 1/2/4/8/9/10 missing. Their later status is not visible in these files.

hypotheses.text: Each adjacent rung (r0→r1→r2→r3→r4) changes either a Q1–Q5 posterior or a preregistered finite-horizon predictive distribution on some history class.
hypotheses.falsifier: An empty witness class, which triggers rung redesign before implementation (Part I D2; Part II §9 as executable searches).
hypotheses.source: Part I D2 (v0.2.3 disjunctive; v0.2.7.1 r0 adjacency); Part II §9 witnesses 1–3, 11
hypotheses.status_now: Satisfied. r0→r1 has an executed witness (tests/test_r0_d2_witness.py). Witness 3 is SATISFIED. Witness 11 is SATISFIED by existence, exactly, and also thresholded on a held-out law (ε = ¼, TV 0.0112), but only in a corner of 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁶ of law mass, with κ as the mechanism. Witnesses 1 and 2 are evidenced by ceiling gaps but not built as enumeration-with-fraction tests (as of 09-01).

hypotheses.text: Lineage is exactly null at full context in both completion disciplines, but becomes informative under truncation (witness 3 stochastic, witness 6 FIFO crossover); the sign of Δ_stoch − Δ_FIFO is not precommitted.
hypotheses.falsifier: An empty predicted class at the frozen validation horizon. That triggers redesign or rescale, not a filter-bug verdict.
hypotheses.source: Part I D10 (v0.2.4 erratum); d10-lineage-search-prereg-v0.1 (stamped before any posterior)
hypotheses.status_now: Confirmed under preregistration: witnesses 3 and 6 ESTABLISHED in C0b, and the interaction is positive in every informative cell. In C1 the lineage rung is 'informative and collapsed' (max 0.0037–0.0066 bits < δ) on straight-line laws; on looping C1′ (40,8,2) r3→r4 is above δ (0.014 canonical, 0.02 corpus per contract).

hypotheses.text: Within-bucket order carries information: shuffled vs. ordered delivery at matched bucket latency changes a posterior on a noncommuting bucket.
hypotheses.falsifier: No noncommuting bucket where order mode changes a posterior (witness 7 empty), or a filter/enumerator mismatch on the shuffled channel.
hypotheses.source: Part I D8 v0.2.2; Part II §4, §9 witness 7; D8 attribution prereg
hypotheses.status_now: Witness 7 SATISFIED in C0b and C1. Prereg predictions P3a and P3b PASS. The C1 ε = 1 cells are collapsed under δ. The shuffled channel is not visible as a learner condition in the files read here.

hypotheses.text: D4: the sparsest rung's exact-filter support stays within a frozen hardware budget. D6: the world excludes group-word-problem and permutation-composition update structure, so the representation gap does not absorb an expressivity term.
hypotheses.falsifier: D4: budget violation, in which case the world shrinks and the ladder is never changed. D6: the audit finds a known-hard update structure in some scheduler condition.
hypotheses.source: Part I D4, D6; Part II §7 and §10; d4-budget-freeze-v0.1 (+ E2, E3)
hypotheses.status_now: D4 MEASURED, not violated. The exit-law pass was brought under the E3 line by interning (about 5 GB against 8 GB). D6's hazard audit (§10 scope) is not reported as a completed deliverable in the files read, so its status is unknown here.

hypotheses.text: Headline Q5 binding generalization: held-out episode-level assignments over familiar tokens, with an exchangeable, counterbalanced split. Lexical generalization is a separate robustness test.
hypotheses.falsifier: Model fails the binding-generalization split relative to its exact ceiling. Per the 2607.19379 warning, any condition requiring arithmetic over episode-random names is a learnability boundary.
hypotheses.source: Part I D3 (v0.2.1/v0.2.2); proposal §6.3; binding is Milestone 4 in proposal §11, so its placement in paper 1 is ambiguous
hypotheses.status_now: The exact side has a bridge: Part II v0.2.9 corpus track, with the lemma executable over all four entity types per 2026-09-18 commits. No binding-split or lexical-split learner evaluation is visible in these files; see learner note. The contract §3 leaves open whether paper 1's headline is the identity axis or the interface ladder.

hypotheses.text: Preregistered held-out predictions P1–P5 on fresh laws at frozen thresholds (e.g. P1: r2 = r3 = r4 sync, r1 later; P5: divergent-class prevalence).
hypotheses.falsifier: As scored against the written predictions.
hypotheses.status_now: 1 PASS (P1, criterion passed but stated mechanism wrong), 3 FAIL (P2 inverted, P3 wrong law, P5b prevalence jump), 1 ill-posed (P4). P5a PASS. Failures are traced to writing-time errors. Confirmatory record is mixed and honestly reported.

cut_commitments: Paper 1 = Milestones 1–3 plus the belief-geometry slice of Milestone 5. Factorization/coupling (RQ3, H4, M4 coupled families) = paper 2. Exposure/causal use (RQ4, H6, patching, residual vs logits) = paper 3. Formal mathematics = later replication domain. Committed before implementation; 'hold the line' (CLAUDE.md; proposal §11, §13 'Overextended first paper').

One computational world in paper 1 (proposal §11). Rule-regime variation, real kernel traces, architecture comparisons, and state-space-model baselines stay extensions (§13; §7.3 says an SSM comparison is not required).

M1 before any transformer: exact filter validated bit-for-bit against an independent enumerator (two-path firewall); observability and synchronization characterized per interface; divergent (immediate-agree/later-diverge) classes exhibited (Part I deliverables 3–5, exit clause).

Interface ladder as controlled single-increment rungs over a fixed generator: r0 kind-only (added v0.2.7.1), r1 actor, r2 +object, r3 +related, r4 +lineage. Fixed D5 schema with MASKED. Controls: entropy-matched irrelevant field conditional on EVENT_KIND, and a redundant field (D2, §6.1). D8 order mode {ordered, shuffled} crossed with content rungs.

Context as epistemic access: offset-unanchored truncation windows with a derived (not stipulated) prior (Part II §2). TIME_CLASS anchoring is a maskable field. Model rows under shift only per the §2(e) shifted-reference rule.

Entity pool much larger than entity count; per-episode naming; binding vs. lexical generalization as separate named tests; exchangeable binding split (D3). The ceiling a model is compared to is the corpus-track (pattern-observer) ceiling, with the canonical track reported beside, labelled (Part II v0.2.9 observer decision).
Deterministic workloads, with stochasticity only in scheduler (ε-policy) and device (queue-level hazard p). The Q4 irreducible term is reported separately (D1, D9, D10).
Support-bound co-design: the world shrinks, never the ladder. D4 budget frozen before curves (D4/D9 precedence).
Thresholds frozen by a second stamp: δ = δ_sync = Δ_τ = 0.01 bits, δ_p as a reporting axis. m = 2, W = 4/8, 𝒯 frozen (Part II v0.2.4/v0.2.5).
Exit law: looping C1′ at (T_ep, L, B) = (40, 8, 2), both statutory ε {1, ½}, full ladder r0–r4 (looping-exit-law-freeze, enacted 2026-09-13).

Evaluation commitments from the proposal in paper 1's scope: KL to the exact Bayes next-event distribution (§8.1); affine alignment to exact posterior/predictive vectors per layer with probe-capacity sensitivity (§8.2); OIR as a proposed, not settled, metric (§8.3); linear/affine/MDL probes primary, nonlinear as sensitivity (§3.4).

Baselines (proposal §7.3): exact Bayes predictor, n-gram/fixed-order Markov, a GRU, untrained-transformer activation controls, shuffled-history and field-permutation controls. Splits across generative factors (§7.2).
From-scratch, single RTX 4090 + Threadripper, no pretrained models, every component inspectable (proposal §7.1, §12; CLAUDE.md).
Methodological posture: exploration instrument; OTS-stamped trace; preregister only confirmatory tests when ready (CLAUDE.md). Multiple seeds around thresholds and primary comparisons (§6.5, M6).

Re-run a focused literature review immediately before any priority claim leaves the repository (CLAUDE.md; both literature notes). Per the 2026-09-18 check: write the query-class gap-3 definition before the first model-versus-ceiling number is reported, even though gap-3 experiments stay in paper 3.
Scope guard: M1 establishes identifiability and instrument validity, not prevalence in production telemetry (Part I).

prior_art.ref: Li et al., Othello-GPT, arXiv:2210.13382
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Next-token models trained on move sequences learn board-state representations that are decodable and causally active (interventions change predictions). Complete move histories largely determine state, so there is no observation gap.

prior_art.ref: Hazineh, Zhang, Chiu, arXiv:2310.07582
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Othello-GPT world state is linearly decodable, and linear interventions are causally implicated in next-move prediction.

prior_art.ref: Shai et al., Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry, arXiv:2405.15943 (NeurIPS 2024)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: For hidden-Markov-generated data, transformer residual streams linearly represent exact Bayesian belief-state (mixed-state) geometry, including distinctions relevant to longer futures but not to the immediate next token. This is the closest conceptual competitor per proposal §2. Generators are small; there is no manipulation of observation interface, context truncation, binding, or coupling.

prior_art.ref: Piotrowski, Riechers, Filan, Shai, arXiv:2502.01954 (ICML 2025)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Constrained belief updates explain the geometric structures seen in transformer representations of hidden-state processes.

prior_art.ref: Chawla, Hall, Lovato, MetaOthello, arXiv:2602.23164 (ICML 2026)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: A single transformer organizes multiple world models with shared syntax but different rules or tokenizations, with causal transfer. It varies the generator, which is the inverse of Yupi's move (vary the observation over a fixed generator). Multiple rules alone are therefore not a contribution.

prior_art.ref: Shai et al., Transformers Learn Factored Representations, arXiv:2602.02385
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Transformers show a bias toward factorized subspaces even when factorization sacrifices predictive fidelity. This is paper-2 territory.

prior_art.ref: Shalizi & Crutchfield, Computational Mechanics, cond-mat/9907176; Littman, Sutton, Singh, Predictive Representations of State (NIPS 2001)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Canonical predictive state (causal states; predictive-state representations) defined through distributions over future observations. These supply the targets and ceilings; they are not competitors.

prior_art.ref: Mason & Anand, Epistemic Observability in Language Models, arXiv:2603.20531
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Output-only (text) supervision cannot distinguish grounded from fabricated outputs, or verify epistemic states, under stated bounded-supervision assumptions. Yupi is framed as its constructive empirical complement.

prior_art.ref: Bayesian wind tunnels (Misra/Dalal group): arXiv:2512.22471, 2607.19379, 2512.23752
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Exact-posterior-ceiling environments are an actively published named method, with transformers reproducing exact posteriors to 10⁻³–10⁻⁴ bits in abstract math worlds. No interface variation, no gap decomposition, not systems. The 'world with exact ceilings' claim is taken. Note: Part I D3 cites arXiv:2607.19379 for the finding that per-episode symbol relabeling is scale-invariantly fatal when the statistic requires computing over symbol identities but harmless for relational key-matching. A judge should confirm that attribution, since the lit review lists 2607.19379 as a wind-tunnel paper.

prior_art.ref: Aswadi, Ma, Wei, Predictive Monte Carlo, arXiv:2607.17060
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: A transformer's implicit prior/posterior can be recovered from output behavior alone. Immediate logits are provably lossy (distinct posteriors share predictive means), and infinite rollouts are complete under c.i.d. idealizations. This is gap-3 territory, relevant to paper 3's definition, not paper 1.

prior_art.ref: Markovian circuit tracing, arXiv:2605.20824 (authorship unverified)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Excess-loss-over-Bayes measurement, belief probing, and counterfactual patching validated against exact HMM counterfactuals, on flat HMMs. No interfaces, no three-way decomposition.

prior_art.ref: Brenner, Knösche, Scherf, Grid Walkers, arXiv:2603.16689
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Belief geometry in a structured-ish grid world, with architecture (transformer vs RNN) as a variable and differing geometry at matched accuracy. No interface axis, no decomposition.

prior_art.ref: Siems et al., state reveals in code traces, arXiv:2602.14814
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: The nearest neighbour to interface variation: the density of 'state reveals' in training data is varied, and capability degrades as reveals sparsen (one-dimensional, no ceilings). It also shows 265M from-scratch transformers failing S₅ permutation-composition tracking even under dense observation, an expressivity failure that motivates the D6 hazard audit.

prior_art.ref: Dalla Riva, arXiv:2604.05469
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Cross-entropy decomposed as irreducible entropy floor plus a JS excess term in small 'laboratory organism' LMs. Two terms only; no simulator posteriors; no interface axis. The 'excess loss over Bayes' framing is taken.

prior_art.ref: Boyd, Rosas et al. transducer decomposition cluster: arXiv:2512.02193, 2504.04608; Cifuentes arXiv:2608.20428
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Composition/decomposition theory for world models; stability of minimal transducer representations under I/O-interface perturbation. Threatens paper 2, not paper 1. 'Interface' there means transducer I/O, not the observation channel.

prior_art.ref: Xu et al., V-information, arXiv:2002.10689
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: The existing formal language for information usable under computational constraints. The accessible-representation gap should be stated in these terms.

prior_art.ref: Kuo et al., arXiv:2510.22039 (NeurIPS 2025)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Equal task performance with different belief fidelity in meta-RL, a precedent for representation–performance dissociation (a cousin of gap 2).

prior_art.ref: Wu, Geiger, Millière, arXiv:2505.20896
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Variable-binding mechanism analysis in transformers. It does not evaluate held-out binding against exact posteriors.

prior_art.ref: Probing practice: arXiv:2502.16681; arXiv:2408.15510
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Tuned linear/MLP probe baselines outperform or match SAE analyses. Causal interventions should report completeness and selectivity. These are methodology obligations, not competitors.

prior_art.ref: Balcells, Lee, Rastogi, Riechers, Shai, Poncini, arXiv:2609.17376 (Sep 15 2026)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Pretrained open LLMs prompted with HMM data develop linearly decodable belief-state geometry in-context (probe R² 0.83–0.99), and subspace interventions move predictions. Not from-scratch, no interface axis, no ceilings-as-decomposition.

prior_art.ref: Ray, Riechers, Shai, 'The geometry of nonergodic composition', belief-updates.pub blog (Sep 9 2026; no arXiv id)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: From-scratch transformers on a direct sum of two Mess3 HMMs, with exact beliefs recovered ('two telescoping cones', R² ≈ 0.985). States in prose that the geometry carries more distinctions than next-token prediction implies, which is gap 3 in words. This is the Simplex item closest to Yupi; the literature check says it must be differentiated explicitly on the interface axis.

prior_art.ref: Wen, Liu, Zhou, Zeng, Su, arXiv:2609.11132 (Sep 10 2026)
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: Theorem in a stationary symmetric Gaussian HMM: an unbounded gap between belief update maps coexists with vanishing predictive KL. Internal divergence is analytically invisible at immediate outputs. This forces the exposure gap to be defined against a query class, and it bears on how paper 1 words any 'model at the ceiling' claim.

prior_art.ref: Shin et al., arXiv:2608.30692; Jerpelea arXiv:2608.26887; ObserverBench arXiv:2609.03026; Mechanistic Tomography arXiv:2608.19338; Carmichael arXiv:2604.24801
prior_art.what_it_already_shows: In order: partial observability with exact hidden ground truth in a video shell game (no ceilings, no interface axis); planted-latent belief tests in LLM text; 'observer' as a control-oriented probe; designed measurement of the model; 'observability' as detectability of confident errors. These are motivation or terminology-collision citations only. Paper 1 needs a one-sentence disambiguation of 'observability'.

charter.drift_from_charter:

novelty.reason: Anyone who knows the Othello-GPT setup will expect this. The kernel's only stochastic choices are which thread runs and completion vs stage B, and both show up in the next record's (kind, actor). So a full log that starts from a known reset determines the state; that is the Othello case, where complete histories fix the board. The proof is an induction on labelled transitions, and anyone who has written a simulator would take the result for granted. The r0 exception (kind-only, with ACTOR masked) is also what you would predict: hide the label on the only stochastic branch and ambiguity comes back. For paper 1 this is a design fact, not a result. It tells the reader why the interface and context manipulations have to run through truncation, windowing or D8 shuffling, and why full context is the zero on both axes. It deserves one sentence or a lemma in the methods or instrument section, with the three load-bearing dependencies stated as design constraints: D9 cursor canonicalization, I5 with lowest-free request ids, and deterministic handoff wake. As a contribution it teaches an ML or interpretability reader nothing new. It is not really a demo of the instrument working either. It is a sanity property of the world's design, and it actually weakens any claim that the interface axis matters in the untruncated regime. Two points matter inside the project: it stops a C1 full-context build that would have been wasted, and it puts the truncation machinery on the critical path. Neither changes what a reader learns.
novelty.nearest_prior: Li et al., Othello-GPT arXiv:2210.13382: complete move histories determine state, so there is no observation gap at full context. More generally, a known initial state plus every stochastic choice labelled in the emitted record gives deterministic state reconstruction (standard POMDP/HMM reasoning; in computational-mechanics terms the process is fully synchronizing from reset).

novelty.reason:
I'd call this project-internal. The rung partitions satisfy n_1 = n_4 exactly when U = T_ep − L ≤ 2, and that follows from how Yupana formats its traces. From reset, the first two records carry no fields. The note's own proof sketch covers the other half: the higher-rung fields in the visible suffix are deterministic functions of history. So if the dropped prefix holds no masked content, the finer telemetry has nothing left to tell apart, and the partitions coincide. An ML or interpretability reader would expect that once the mechanism is stated. The general principle, that extra observation fields are redundant whenever they can be computed from what is already visible, is standard sufficiency or data-processing reasoning. None of it tells us anything about learners, representations, or the three-gap decomposition. The threshold of 2 is a detail of this simulator's C1/C0b reset sequence, and the note says the rule is an argument for C1, is only consistent with C0b, is not a theorem, and fails for r0.

It is valuable internally. Checking n_windows for equality costs nothing, it keeps a structural exact zero from being reported as a finding about interfaces, and it keeps the near-full-context zeros separate from the sub-δ collapse horizons. That makes it the kind of boundary recheck the house rules ask for. In the paper it belongs in the methods section or an appendix, as a sanity check in the instrument description. It should not be presented as a result. It doesn't qualify as "novel as an instrument demo" either, because it is a property of how this trace format is encoded, not evidence that the instrument measures something a reader would not have predicted.
novelty.nearest_prior: This is standard sufficient-statistic and data-processing reasoning. When observation fields are deterministic functions of the visible history, adding them doesn't refine the belief partition. Among the listed priors, the closest framing is the observation ceilings from Shalizi & Crutchfield causal states and Littman/Sutton/Singh predictive state representations. Siems et al. arXiv:2602.14814 is the nearest one-dimensional precedent for varying observation density, but it does not have this structural degeneracy.

novelty.reason: The split is total = Σ_s b_w(s)H(f(s)) + gap (c1-q4-ceilings §71). This is the standard decomposition H(Y|O) = H(Y|S) + I(Y;S|O), which holds when the target depends on the observation only through the state. "Conservation" is not an empirical result. By the tower property, the law-weighted mean of the irreducible term, E_O[Σ_s b(s|O)H(Y|s)], equals E_S[H(Y|S)] for every observation rung, so it has to be rung-invariant. Seeing it come out float-identical is a correctness check on the filter and the bookkeeping, not a lesson. Three other points follow from the setup. (1) Gap = 0 under full context follows from the ceiling definition. (2) A positive irreducible term for a stochastic wake target is guaranteed by design. (3) "Interface moves only the gap" restates Shai-style/computational-mechanics ceilings plus the data-processing inequality, and exact-ceiling environments are already published (Bayesian wind tunnels). Calling it "the first nonzero full-context ceiling" only means something inside the project's M1 target sequence. The one quantity that tells a reader something about this world is the size of the windowed observation gap (about 0.11–0.40 bits, larger at L=2 than at L=4). That sits with the instrument-demo interface-ladder results, not here, and v0.2 has already withdrawn its ranking against the state-predicate targets. The numbers are also from the buggy-kernel exploratory runs and predate the v0.2.4 stamp. At most this deserves one methods sentence ("the irreducible floor is rung-invariant, as it must be, verified to float precision"), not a finding.

novelty.reason: The direction is exactly what the standard view predicts. In a finite system with a bounded mixing time, a longer conditioning window lowers posterior state entropy, and the gain is largest when the window is short (L=2 vs 4 events). Richer observation content per event also helps, but by less once the coarsest rung already reports the transition kind. A reader who knows computational mechanics (synchronization, and entropy decreasing with block length) or Siems et al.'s reveal-density result would expect context to matter more than per-event content at L=2 to 4. The ratio (1.92 vs 0.25 bits) is a fact about one configuration (C1, T_ep=14, B=2, two noise levels), not a general law. It is also not separated from the window-geometry choices themselves. L=2 is a very aggressive truncation, so the comparison partly measures how short L=2 is. Several things limit how far it can be pushed as a lesson. It is buggy-kernel exploratory: corrected-kernel magnitudes drift by up to 0.041 at (14,4,2), which leaves the qualitative ratio intact but is still a caveat. It was already corrected once, because v0.1 compared across two horizons. It is scoped to "these laws". The exactness does not change what is learned: the lesson "context dominates" would survive a rough estimate. Its real value is internal and methodological. It tells the paper how to read, and possibly where to place, the interface-axis manipulations. For example: report interface effects at matched L, and pick L large enough that content differences are not swamped. That makes it a framing or design-control observation for the paper's methods section, not a standalone contribution. At most it is a one-line demonstration that the instrument can put both axes on the same bit scale.

A reader who knows computational mechanics would expect the headline. A small finite stochastic world with ~14-record traces synchronizes to its hidden state within a few observations, and observer-ambiguity mass falls fast with context length. That is the standard synchronization behaviour Travers & Crutchfield describe for exact and asymptotically synchronizing processes. It follows that richer observation rungs lose their advantage once the weakest rung has synchronized.

Two parts are specific: the ambiguity that no rung can split is mostly program-counter-only, and the only residual a rung can reach is lock ownership. Both are facts about how Yupana's rungs are defined, with nothing that carries over to other settings. Ruling out exhaustion is a sanity check.

The result matters inside the project. It shows the r1–r4 interface ladder has no range beyond ~8–10 records in C1, so the world has to change before the interface axis can show anything. For paper 1 it is design rationale: at most a sentence or a methods footnote saying why the world was redesigned, not a finding.

Reservation on exactness: separating 'ambiguity no interface could resolve' from 'ambiguity a richer interface could resolve' exactly is a use of the instrument. The substantive version of that point will come from the post-intervention world, not this collapse census.
novelty.nearest_prior: Travers & Crutchfield on synchronization to hidden state in finite HMMs (exact and asymptotic synchronization rates); computational mechanics causal-state framework (Shalizi & Crutchfield, cond-mat/9907176)

novelty.reason: This finding does not clear the bar of teaching something new. The claim has two parts. (1) If you hide which thread performed each action, some ambiguity never resolves, even at full context. (2) Every other rung (r1 to r4) converges by L≈12, so masking ACTOR is the only step with range at long context. A reader who knows HMM non-identifiability, Othello-GPT (full histories fix state), or Siems et al. (sparser state reveals mean worse tracking) would predict both parts. A kind-only projection of a multi-thread world is a many-to-one channel. Threads whose programs share kind multisets (threads 0 and 2 here) cannot be told apart from kinds alone. So a non-decaying posterior entropy of a few bits is the default expectation, not a surprise. Part (2) is really the earlier ladder-collapse result (r1 to r4 lose range by L=12), restated from the other side. The exact numbers (2.577 / 2.375-bit plateau, 0.49 to 0.60-bit step) do not carry a lesson by being exact. The one mechanistic explanation that might have been interesting, a clean permutation entropy over kind-indistinguishable roles, was withdrawn (Part II v0.2.7.1). The replacement is only a support classification: about 80% of ambiguous mass (ε=1) sits in supports whose states differ even after anonymizing threads to their signatures. The note calls it that itself, not a decomposition of the entropy. So the paper cannot currently say what the plateau is made of. The "teaches" line, that this ties the interface axis to naming/binding, is a design consequence for the project. It rescues M2's interface axis from the r1 to r4 collapse and moves the naming bridge up the list. It is not a finding for an outside reader. It is also exploratory: r0 is an instrument extension, not a statutory rung, the full gate was not run, and the ceilings are not statutory. Use in paper 1: as an instrument/design fact (the axis needs an identity-masking rung to have range past about 8 records), stated in one or two sentences. It should not be presented as a result. It could become interesting only if a trained model's gap at r0 turns out to behave differently from its gap at r1 to r4, or if the naming-bridge work shows r0 ambiguity matching the random-naming mixture. Neither has been measured.
novelty.nearest_prior: Standard HMM/POMDP non-identifiability under many-to-one observation (aliasing), with Siems et al. arXiv:2602.14814 (sparser state reveals degrade tracking) and Li et al. Othello-GPT arXiv:2210.13382 (complete histories determine state) bracketing the expectation. Internally it restates the r1-r4 ladder collapse (full-context-injectivity-note-v0.1.md) from the other side.

Its content is allocator state (lowest-free request ids), not causal matching: the completion-matching channel contributes exactly zero at every law, structurally because under I5 with ACTOR visible every completion is matched to its issue by ACTOR alone. support.problems:
I could not refute the core claim. Every number reproduces from the committed raws, and the corrected-kernel raws (2026-08-20) give the same r3→r4 values to 5 d.p. (0.00128 / 0.00173 / 0.00376 at ε=1) and exactly the same id surplus (1.439e-4 r1, 9.350e-5 r4), so the buggy-kernel banner does not threaten these numbers. The v0.4 structural argument (I5 plus visible ACTOR) was audited as sound in request-id-design-question v0.3. Statutory Q4, which was unimplemented when the claim was written, was measured later at ≤0.0006 bits r3→r4, so "every declared query ≤0.0013" still holds. No house-rule violation: the surplus zeros at (12,2,2) and (14,4,2) are exact 0.0 in the raws and were checked by enumeration, and the matching zero rests on a structural argument, not on a float sum. Six problems with how the claim is stated:

(1) "vs 0.13–0.20 for each other rung" is wrong at the low end. At (14,4,2), ε=1, r2→r3 = 0.1174 (buggy raw) and 0.1115 (corrected). The true ε=1 range is 0.117–0.195 (buggy) or 0.112–0.179 (corrected). The error comes from the source note's Finding 2. The comparison also holds only at ε=1: at ε=1/2 the other rungs are 0.047–0.105.

(2) "≤0.0003 at ε=1/2" understates (14,2,2), where the value is 0.000347. That rounds to 0.0003 but is above it.

(3) Stale labels. The claim uses v0.1 labels. Under the v0.2 relabel, "Q3" is thread-only Q3thr and "Q3ids" is statutory Q3. The surplus should read Q3 − Q3thr. Both move almost equally r3→r4 (at (14,2,2), 0.00373 for Q3 and 0.00368 for Q3thr), so "lands on Q3" is true under either label.

(4) "Its content is allocator state (lowest-free ids)" needs a caveat. Allocator state is the channel. But almost all of what r4 adds is at the thread level (Q3thr moves nearly as much as Q3), so the id tells you which threads are in flight and in what order; recovering the id label itself is a small share (the surplus is about 1e-4). D10 (C0b, v0.1.1) formally separates "allocator-label recovery" from "lineage informs issuing-thread order" and finds both mechanisms, so "allocator leakage, not causal matching" is right about matching but too coarse about what the content is. D10 v0.1.1 item 4 also records that C1's r3→r4 classes are nonempty but below δ (up to ~0.0037 bits at T_ep=14, 0.0066 at 16). That is consistent with the claim, and a useful update to cite.

(5) The rung-geometry decomposition (the "every split differs only in lineage fields, completion adds nothing" mechanical check) has no corrected-kernel rerun; its banner says so explicitly. The matching zero rests on the structural argument, not on that measurement.

(6) "Every law" for the matching zero means every law of C1 as configured, under I5 with ACTOR visible at all rungs. It is not a statement about worlds or masks that relax either.

novelty.reason: This is a finding about how the instrument's own rung ladder was designed. It does not teach an ML or interpretability reader anything new about learners or about observability. The main result is that the lineage fields add almost nothing (about 0.001 to 0.004 bits against 0.13 to 0.20 for the other rungs). What little they add is allocator state leaking through lowest-free id assignment, and completion matching contributes exactly zero. The notes say that zero follows from the rules: under I5 (at most one outstanding request) with ACTOR visible, every completion is matched to its issue by ACTOR alone. So the zero follows from how the world was defined and did not need to be measured. The general point, that identifiers assigned by a deterministic allocator leak allocator state and so a field meant to carry X ends up carrying Y, is a familiar leakage and shortcut confound. Readers who know systems will also expect it, since lowest-free allocation is a known side channel. The project's own entity-naming constraint in CLAUDE.md, which draws identifiers per episode from a large pool, already anticipates this. None of the listed prior art (Shai et al., Othello-GPT, wind tunnels, Siems et al. on state reveals) covers it, but that is because it is a schema-design detail, not a new phenomenon. Several things weaken it as a paper claim. The magnitudes are tiny: the id surplus is about 1e-4 bits and only appears at (14,2,2). The notes have been corrected repeatedly: v0.1's headline was refuted, v0.3's stated cause was replaced in v0.4, and two predictions about the id surplus were each half wrong. Both notes also carry a buggy-kernel banner, and no corrected-kernel rerun exists yet for the rung-geometry quantities. For paper 1 this belongs in the methods or instrument-validation section: a warning that record-schema identifiers must not encode allocator policy, and a reason to either relax I5 or mask ACTOR if lineage is meant to measure causal matching. It should not be listed as a contribution.
novelty.nearest_prior: The project's own entity-identifier design constraint (per-episode identifiers drawn from a large pool, CLAUDE.md), together with the general shortcut and leakage literature on probes and datasets. Among the listed prior art, the closest is Siems et al., arXiv:2602.14814, which varies how many state reveals appear in the trace, but none covers identifier-allocator leakage because it is an instrument-design detail.

novelty.reason: An ML or interpretability reader will take it as given that how much an observation channel is worth depends on the query. Which field matters depends on what you are asking about. A per-query mutual-information table across interface rungs shows exactly that, and it is a standard consequence of Bayesian decision/value-of-information reasoning. The same goes for the finding that most state entropy sits in fields no query targets (pc, rr_cursor). Queries are coarse-grainings of the state, so H(query) is much smaller than H(state) by construction. The one mildly non-obvious detail is that a field can inform a query without appearing in its answer. For example, Q4proxy's r2→r3 gain is 94.9% BLOCK.related even though the owner is not in the answer. But any reader who knows computational mechanics or belief-state filtering expects this: in an HMM, observations inform latent variables by pinning down trajectories, and Shai et al. already stress distinctions that are not in the immediate answer. So the lesson here is not the exactness itself. The per-field attribution is a nice demonstration of the instrument (exact, additive, field-level ceiling decomposition), and it can serve as a methods illustration or supplementary table showing that the ladder has to be read per query. It should not be a headline result. Further caveats weaken it: the note carries a buggy-kernel erratum (qualitative structure reportedly survives, magnitudes drift by up to 0.041 at (14,4,2)); statutory Q4 is unimplemented, so Q4proxy is a proxy; the v0.2 correction found the per-pair Q5 dominance does not hold uniformly; and the magnitudes are small (a largest query ceiling of 0.60 bits). If it goes in at all, it goes in as supporting instrument evidence, the kind that 'novel-as-instrument-demo' would cover at best. It is not a claim that teaches readers something they did not know.
novelty.nearest_prior: Standard value-of-information and coarse-graining reasoning. Within the listed prior art, the nearest is Shai et al. arXiv:2405.15943 on belief-state distinctions beyond the immediate answer, together with Siems et al. arXiv:2602.14814 (one-dimensional variation of observation density, with capability depending on the reveals).

novelty.reason:
This finding is a correction to the project's own pipeline, not a result about learned models or observability. Its stated lesson is that a renormalized-subsample mean estimates nothing, so exact exhaustive computation with independent cross-checking is needed. Any ML or statistics reader already treats that as basic practice. Selection-biased estimates of posterior-support size are a known failure mode, and exact enumeration is the obvious fix in a finite world. The Bayesian wind-tunnel papers already take that "exact ceilings" posture.

The numbers that survive are useful for the instrument's feasibility but teach a reader nothing new:
- **The budget does not bind.** The worst step has 144 or 243 transitions against a budget of 70,000, and the maximum support is 28 against 20,000. That confirms the design constraint "co-design against a support bound" was met. It belongs in an appendix or methods sentence about computational feasibility.
- **The rung ordering is small and unsurprising.** Supports run r1 > r2 > r3 ≈ r4, all between about 1.3 and 1.6. Richer interfaces giving smaller or equal posterior support is what the standard view predicts.
- **The max-28 window.** It is invariant across rungs, with a three-way offset posterior and per-component supports of 3/9/16. This is a cautionary instance detail about the instrument.

Status also counts against inclusion. The v0.3 audit withdrew two of the findings. The D9 outcome was downgraded to provisional. The RESET erratum's zero effect was rescued empirically rather than proved. The measurements came from a kernel that had a bug, so they are exploratory.

Recommendation: keep only the corrected exact support table as a supporting feasibility or methods note in paper 1 (support bound verified, exhaustive and cross-checked). Do not frame the sampling-bias episode as a contribution. It is provenance and belongs in the project log.

novelty.reason: The qualitative claim is textbook. Some histories give the same next-symbol distribution but lead to different futures. That is why computational mechanics defines causal states over whole futures, and why predictive-state representations use tests longer than one step. Shai et al. (2405.15943) say outright that belief geometry keeps distinctions that don't matter for the next token. PMC (2607.17060) proves immediate logits are lossy, and Wen et al. (2609.11132) prove an unbounded belief gap can sit alongside vanishing predictive KL. A reader who knows this literature would predict exact pairs like IO_COMPLETE;ACQUIRE vs IO_COMPLETE;RELEASE. The rest of the finding is weak. The prevalence numbers (pair_prob 5e-8 to 3e-5 at L=2, about 1e-3 at L=4; divergent mass 31-42% at L=4 and 95-98% at full context) describe this simulator only and don't generalize. They were computed under the buggy kernel, which the note banners, and were drifted rather than recomputed. The parameters m, W and δ were not frozen, and the explanatory mechanism ("siblings") was withdrawn. The note itself says exact equality is a knife-edge criterion, so the headline counts depend on that knife-edge, and the fix (δ-close/Δ-apart) is ordinary practice. At most it deserves one sentence in paper 1: a finite, exact example that supports defining the exposure gap against a query class. Gap 3 belongs to paper 3 anyway. It is not a contribution in its own right.

novelty.reason: The question only makes sense for the project's own "divergent mass" statistic: pairs of observation windows whose next-record law is the same but whose τ functional differs, compared across the r_obs/r_pred rungs of C1. An ML or interpretability reader has never held the belief that this statistic is monotone, so showing it is not monotone overturns nothing they know. The counterexample is also elementary. P-next and τ are linear in the belief, and a coarse window's belief is a mixture of its refined pieces, so an equality between two mixtures can hold while no pair of components matches. Anyone who knows that "refining a partition need not preserve equalities between mixtures" (the same kind of fact behind Simpson's paradox and the lossy predictive means in Aswadi et al.) would predict the note's 0.18 → 0.095 example. The measured ledger is carefully done: turnover rather than inheritance, a creation-to-loss ratio of about 4:1, and new-within sibling pairs. But the numbers are tiny (1e-6 to 1e-5), limited to δ_p=0 and r_pred=r1, cover two laws on a single path, and give no general reason why creation wins. It corrects the project's own earlier 24/24 pattern (open question 1 of c1-divergent-grid) and keeps an internal "theorem" from being overclaimed. That makes it hygiene, not a result for readers. The finding itself is tagged gap=exposure, cut=paper3, so it falls outside paper 1 under the committed cut in any case. Recommendation: at most one footnote in the exposure-gap paper noting that observer-monotonicity is empirical and not structural. It should not appear in paper 1.
novelty.nearest_prior: Elementary fact that linear-functional equalities between mixtures are not preserved under partition refinement (Simpson's-paradox-style aggregation reversal). The closest recorded item is Aswadi, Ma, Wei arXiv:2607.17060, which shows immediate predictive means are lossy because distinct posteriors share them. Internally, the finding answers open question 1 of docs/c1-divergent-grid-v0.1.md.

findings.claim: Proposed definition: the exposure gap is G(Q) = I₁ − I₂(Q), the V-information about Z_t recoverable from activations by constrained probes minus that recoverable from output distributions under a declared query class Q (depth, breadth, adaptivity, channel, functional family), with a sampling gap S(Q) = I₂(Q) − I₃(Q); the four-observer telescope makes all gaps restricted-observer information differences. Addendum 2026-09-04: exposure is a policy under instruction for frontier models (Astra reshapes CoT 60.9% of the time vs 16.1% / 1.7%), so Yupi's trace-only models measure the no-incentive floor.
findings.teaches: Relativizing the exposure gap to observer power removes the data-processing triviality objection and makes the three-gap decomposition uniform, with the probe family V on the representation side mirrored by Q on the output side.
findings.corrections: none found; note is explicitly 'definitions proposed, not settled'; addendum requires v0.2 to index G by production condition as well as Q.

support.problems:
The extraction matches the note. G(Q) = I1 − I2(Q) and S(Q) = I2(Q) − I3(Q) are in the §2 table. The query-class axes are in §3, the Astra figures (60.9% / 16.1% / 1.7%) are in the Addendum, and the addendum's demand that v0.2 index G by production condition is quoted correctly. The note is committed at 58e7e56 (2026-08-11) and the addendum at a4060d5 (2026-09-04). No later correction, retraction or v0.2 exists in docs/. The house rules on prefix-only subsets, boundary rechecks and inert variables do not apply, because no realized-record numbers are involved. The problems are with what the claim and its "teaches" line assert beyond the note's hedges:

(1) G(Q) is not guaranteed to be nonnegative, so it is not a "gap" in the data-processing sense. V-information does not obey the data-processing inequality. The probe family V (linear or MDL-bounded on A_t) and the query class Q (arbitrary functionals of output laws) are not nested. A rich Q can recover more about Z_t than a linear probe on the activations, which makes G negative. The note itself hedges this: terms are nonnegative only "when the access sets are nested in the natural way", and that condition is never stated. It is also internally inconsistent. §3 says that at the idealized ceiling Q_inf, G → 0. But if unbounded rollouts recover the model's full implicit posterior, I2 can approach the model's unrestricted information, and I1 is V-restricted. So G → I1 − I2 ≤ 0, not 0. The "teaches" line says relativization "removes the DPI triviality objection". More precisely, it trades that objection for a sign and nesting condition that is still undefined.

(2) "Makes all gaps restricted-observer information differences" slightly overstates the note. The observation gap uses O0, which has restricted access (h_t) but an unrestricted decoder family. The note's own symmetry claim covers only gaps 2 and 3 (V mirrored by Q).

(3) The note's §2 says each term is "exactly computable in Yupana because the restricted infima are over finite, enumerable measurement families". That is false as written: linear or MDL probe families and continuation functionals are continuous, so I1, I2 and I3 are estimated. Only H(Z_t | h_t) is exact. This is not in the extracted claim, but it undercuts "exact ceilings" for gap 3.

(4) The claim that the addendum "measures the no-incentive floor" rests on the assertion that "everything a frontier model's training adds can only raise it". That assertion is unsupported. Instructability cuts both ways, since a model can be told to expose more. And a trace-only model in Yupana and a frontier model are different models on different worlds, so neither has a G that bounds the other's. The addendum itself says a small model may have no exposure policy at all. "Floor" is a framing, not a measured or proven bound.

(5) The Astra figures cannot be verified from the repo. They are quoted second-hand from a system card that Tony quoted, and they match the addendum text.

(6) Status: still v0.1 and exploratory. The D7 consistency check against this observer hierarchy is UNBUILT and was never performed (m1-exit-evidence-map-2026-09-01 row 4.7). literature-check-2026-09-18 says the gap-3 definition must now cite Wen et al. arXiv:2609.11132, which shows immediate-logit exposure is degenerate in principle, and must be written before any model-versus-ceiling number is reported. That revision has not happened. Meanwhile the 2026-09-24 belief-geometry design already reports KL_repr vs KL_out at p0 as "an exposure gap at this position". That is a Q_logit (N=0) point on the lattice, and per the note it must be labelled as such, not read as G.

The sampling gap is S(Q) = I2(Q) − I3(Q). Gaps 2 and 3 thus become restricted-observer information differences, with Q on the output side mirroring V on the representation side. novelty.reason: This is a definition, not a result, and it belongs to paper 3, not paper 1. The core move is to measure the exposure gap relative to a declared query class, with every gap stated as a restricted-observer V-information difference. A reader who knows the listed prior art would expect that move. Xu et al. (2002.10689) already supply the restricted-observer information language. Wen et al. (2609.11132) prove that internal divergence can be invisible at immediate outputs, which forces a query-class definition. Aswadi, Ma & Wei (2607.17060) bracket the space from both ends: a single immediate query is lossy, and idealized infinite rollouts are complete. The note itself cites these as the reasons the repair is needed. Taking the V side (probe family) and mirroring it with a Q side (query family) is therefore the obvious construction once those papers are read. The "four-observer telescope" is tidy and useful inside the project because it makes the three-gap decomposition uniform and computable, but it gives an ML or interpretability reader nothing they would not reach themselves. Q has not been operationalized into a lattice with measured values in Yupana, so there is also no instrument demonstration yet. The 2026-09-04 addendum (exposure as a policy for frontier models, with Astra's CoT-reshaping rates) draws on external findings; the only project-side point is that trace-only models measure the no-incentive floor, a scoping remark and not a finding. The note labels itself "definitions proposed, not settled." It could become more than framing only if paper 3 measures G(Q) across query classes in Yupana and finds something surprising in the lattice, for example non-monotonicity in rollout depth or adaptivity. For paper 1, at most a single sentence of framing should carry it forward, pointing ahead to paper 3.

V-information arXiv:2002.10689 and Aswadi/Ma/Wei arXiv:2607.17060 (immediate logits are lossy; infinite rollouts are complete under c.i.d. conditions)

novelty.reason: The evidence docs back the defect itself (audit-adjudication Finding 1 verified three ways, fix d69fa87, erratum v0.1.1 strengthening I2/I6). But it is a bug in the project's own simulator. The lesson drawn from it is standard verification practice, and any ML or interpretability reader, or any systems reader, already knows it. Two implementations that share the same transition code have a common-mode failure. A differential test between the filter and the enumerator validates inference relative to the kernel, not the kernel's semantics. Catching a wrong transition law takes an independent specification or invariants: N-version programming, the oracle problem, and model-checking practice all say this. No reader learns anything about transformers, belief geometry, observability, or the gap decomposition from it. The exact contamination masses (up to about 44% at C0a T=14, about 1.75% at C1 eps=1 T=14) matter only for which of the project's own artifacts are trustworthy. They do not generalize. The finding still belongs in paper 1, but in the methods/limitations and internal-validity disclosure (the relabeling of buggy-kernel artifacts, the I1-I6 invariant suite, the corrected 58-state count). It should not be presented as a contribution or as something the paper teaches. One caveat is worth a sentence at most. The Bayesian wind-tunnel literature treats 'exact posterior' as ground truth without discussing that the posterior is exact only relative to a correctly implemented generator. A single cautionary line to that effect is reasonable framing, not a novel result.
novelty.nearest_prior: Standard software-verification knowledge (N-version programming / common-mode failure, e.g. Knight & Leveson 1986; the test-oracle problem; differential testing only validates relative to a shared specification). Within the ML prior set, the Bayesian wind tunnels (arXiv:2512.22471, 2607.19379) take generator correctness for granted as the implicit 'exact oracle' assumption, but there is no competing result there to beat.

novelty.reason:
I checked the claim against docs/d1-falsifier-verdict-v0.1.md, Part B formal verdict (2026-09-01). The numbers match, and that section supersedes the conditional text from Aug 20.

What this result actually does is settle the project's own M1 exit clause: it says whether Yupana's ordered telemetry rungs are distinct enough to be worth manipulating. That makes it a calibration of the instrument, not a finding about learners or representations.

The part an ML or interpretability reader could take away is expected from standard filtering and observability reasoning. In a small, finite, mixing world with a window of 14 ticks, a long enough history pins down the posterior over current state whatever the telemetry is. So richer observation interfaces should differ only at short context, and the gaps should shrink as L grows. The specific horizons are artifacts of this world's parameters and of the frozen δ = 0.01, and the r2→r3 horizon is δ-sensitive: its cell sits 1.5×10⁻⁵ below the threshold. None of these values carry over to another setting.

The exact 0.0 gaps at L = 12 and 14 are the one place where exactness shows. But they reflect this world's finite synchronization depth, not a general lesson. The same goes for the lineage rung never separating: it says that rung was badly designed for this world (D10's "informative-and-collapsed" reading). It is not a fact about observation channels in general.

This belongs in paper 1's methods section or an appendix, as the justification for running the interface manipulations at short context (L ≤ 6), where three distinct regimes exist with gaps of 0.04–0.17 bits. It should not be presented as a contribution.

Nearest prior: Siems et al. (arXiv:2602.14814) already show, along one dimension, that sparser state reveals mean less recoverable state. Behind the rest is standard hidden-Markov and filtering theory: posteriors forget their initial conditions, and in an observable finite system a long enough window of observations determines the state.
novelty.nearest_prior: Standard HMM filtering and observability theory (an observable finite system is determined by a long enough observation window; filter stability). Siems et al., arXiv:2602.14814 (one-dimensional density of state reveals).

support.problems:
The theorem half holds. The constraint-(b) half and the headroom numbers are misstated or superseded.

(1) The theorem half stands, with scope limits. At L = T_ep every content rung r1–r4 gives a point mass, so D1's full-context component fired by theorem (commit 0772227). Three limits apply:
- Audit finding 3 restricts it to the role-known structural quotient. It does not cover the formal S_t with sigma, which is not implemented.
- Part II v0.2.7.1 (enacted 2026-09-11) scopes it to r1–r4 explicitly. The kind-only rung r0 is NOT injective at full context: H = 2.577 bits at eps = 1 and 2.375 at eps = 1/2 at (14,14,2). So "the interface axis is degenerate at full context" no longer holds once r0 is on the axis. The claim's own wording (r1–r4) is correct.
- The exhaustive check `scripts/injectivity_check.py` was never rerun after the kernel fix d69fa87 (its only commit is 0772227), and `artifact-status.json` still says "exhaustive checks rerun owed". Indirect corrected-kernel evidence does exist: the corrected (14,14,2) ceilings drift is exactly 0 at L = 14 (d04fbef), and the prediction checker passes the theorem on all 24 committed full-context cells (335eb8d).

(2) "Constraint (b) REFUTED" has been superseded. Part I D4 was amended in the v0.2.7.1 companion. It keeps constraint (b)'s premise, "the sparsest interface produces the fastest posterior-support growth", and re-points the requirement at r0. It records that r0's supports are larger than r1's at every measured C1 context: max support at L = 8 is 64 for r0 vs 28 for r1, and at full context 33 vs 1. The direction of (b) is therefore confirmed. What the evidence shows is only that the budget did not bind at C1 scale: r0 max support is 282. Even that is scale-limited, because larger laws are now refused on memory under D4:
- (40,8,2) pass refused at 13.03 GB and 13.25 GB peak RSS (`exit-clause-40-8-2-note-v0.1.md`).
- (15,15,1) r1–r3 refused at 4.81 GB (`m1-exit-evidence-map-2026-09-01.md`, D4 row, which says re-pricing at characterization scale is still owed).
So "the risk was legibility rather than intractability" is a C1-scale finding, not a property of the world.

(3) Number mix-up in the headroom figure, inherited from the D1 note:
- "Max support 28" is a windowed quantity at WindowLaw(12,6,2), T_ep = 12, L = 6. It is not a full-context number; at full context r1 support is 1. It sits next to the full-context H = 0 claim as if it measured the same regime.

On inert variables: sigma is exactly the variable the kernel never writes, and audit finding 3 correctly excludes it from the theorem's state. The claim needs that scope stated.

novelty.reason: Full-history identifiability of a finite, reset-anchored world with deterministic workloads and near-deterministic transitions is what the standard view predicts. The Othello-GPT line already works from the premise that complete histories determine state, so there is no observation gap. An ML/interp reader would take "point-mass posterior at L = T_ep" as a sanity property of the generator, not a finding. The "teaches" line, that the risk was legibility rather than intractability and that only truncation creates observation gaps, does two things. It refutes the project's own founding constraint (b), and it justifies the window design. Both are project-internal: they matter for the methods section (why context windows are the manipulated variable, and why support stays tractable), not as a contribution. Several things weaken it further. Audit finding 3 limits the theorem to the role-known structural quotient; it is false as stated once σ/episode-local naming enters. "Max support 28 / ~300x headroom" is a pre-fix number that needs repricing. The injectivity checks were owed a rerun. Paper use: one or two sentences in the world/methods description ("at full context the posterior is a point mass on the structural quotient, so every observation gap in this paper comes from truncation"), with the quotient caveat stated. It is not a result claim. The exactness is not itself the lesson here, because a zero gap is the trivially expected ceiling.

(1) "On held-out laws the max is 0.003255 (F3′)" leaves out a held-out family. F1 = (16, L even, 2) is itself a held-out family, added in held-out-confirmation §8 after §3 was written. Its r3→r4 max is 0.006587 (Q3[D0], ε=1, L=2) in c1-sync-sweep-F1-heldout-2026-08-23.json. So 0.003255 is the maximum over F2 and F3′ only. The maximum over all held-out laws is 0.0066, and that is the (16,2,2) figure the claim quotes in its next sentence as if it were separate. D1 Part B carries the same split wording.

(2) The "teaches" line overreaches in two ways.
(a) "Collapsed under any plausible δ" does not hold. At (16,2,2) ε=1 the gap is 0.0066, so any δ between 0.0037 and 0.0066 would not collapse that cell. The empty band (0.003728, 0.046568) is established only for T_ep ∈ {12,14}, L ∈ {2,4}. The rung is collapsed under the frozen δ = 0.01, not under any δ.
(b) "In C1" is wider than what was measured. Every measurement behind the claim is a C1 law with T_ep ≤ 16 and windows starting near reset. deep-truncation-census-v0.1 (2026-09-03, exploratory, corrected kernel) measures C1 itself at horizon 32. There the lineage rung is ABOVE δ:
- Q3[D0] r3→r4 = 0.014 at (32,8,2) ε=1
- 0.009 at (32,8,2) ε=½, sitting at the threshold
- about 0.046 at (32,4,2) ε=1
In C1′, exit-clause-40-8-2-note gives r3→r4 = 0.0142 / 0.0113 at (40,8,2) at the two statutory ε; c1-prime-live-census gives 0.042 / 0.036 at (48,4,2). These later notes do not refute the (14,·,2)/(16,·,2) numbers. They do refute the general lesson that the fourth rung is collapsed in C1. The rung's grip grows enough to cross δ once windows start mid-episode. The new laws are exploratory and not frozen.

Minor: c1-delta-sweep-v0.1.md has a buggy-kernel erratum banner, and a pointer saying no corrected-kernel rerun exists yet. That pointer is stale, because c1-delta-sweep-corrected-2026-08-21.json exists and reproduces all six r3→r4 cell maxima and the 6/6 Q3[D0] argmax exactly. The claim therefore stands on the corrected artifacts.

House rules: no violation found. The exact 0.0 gaps at L=12 and 14 are reported with the float-noise level (≤9e-15) and do not bear on the r3→r4 maximum. No prefix-subset or inert-variable issue applies.
support.corrected_claim:
On the corrected kernel, the lineage rung (r3→r4) never separates by more than 0.003728 bits on (14,·,2), for any L from 2 to 14 and either ε. On held-out laws the maximum is:
- 0.000777 on F2
- 0.003255 on F3′
- 0.006587 on F1 at (16,2,2) ε=1, which is the largest held-out value, below δ = 0.01 but about 1.8× the (14,·,2) maximum.
The argmax is Q3[D0] in all 6/6 δ-sweep cells, and in every held-out family's maximum. The classes are non-empty ("informative and collapsed").

Lesson, correctly scoped: at C1 laws measured from reset with T_ep ≤ 16, the lineage rung adds real information but stays under the frozen δ = 0.01, so it is collapsed at every measured L. It is not collapsed under every plausible δ: a δ between 0.0037 and 0.0066 would leave the (16,2,2) cell uncollapsed. Its grip grows with horizon. At C1 horizon 32 (exploratory, deep-truncation census) and in C1′ at (40,8,2) and (48,4,2), r3→r4 goes above δ (about 0.011–0.046 bits). So "the fourth rung is collapsed in C1" is a statement about short, from-reset horizons, not about C1 in general.

novelty.reason: This finding is a verdict about one rung (r3→r4, request lineage) of the project's own interface ladder, judged against a threshold δ that the project defined for itself. It says that exposing lineage adds a small but nonzero amount of information about hidden state (about 0.004 bits or less on (14,·,2), 0.0066 at (16,2,2)), that this stays below δ, and that it grows with horizon. An ML or interpretability reader would expect all three parts. Extra observation channels cannot lose information and usually add some. A channel that is mostly redundant with what the trace already reveals adds only a sliver. Longer horizons let small per-step differences add up. The exact figures, the failed P3 bound, the withdrawn 'dead region' claim and the Q3[D0] argmax matter for the project's bookkeeping, since they settle whether the fourth rung earns its own condition. None of it is a transferable lesson. The one outside-facing point is that exact posteriors can certify a rung as informative-but-collapsed, a nonzero gap measured to about 10⁻³ bits instead of an estimate lost in noise. That is the instrument doing its normal job (the Bayesian wind-tunnel papers already show exact ceilings at this precision) and is better covered by a finding that shows the full interface ladder. At most this belongs in paper 1 as a line in a table or an appendix note explaining why the ladder is reported with three effective rungs. It should not be headlined.
novelty.nearest_prior: Siems et al. arXiv:2602.14814, where denser 'state reveals' improve capability monotonically (one-dimensional, no ceilings). Bayesian wind tunnels (arXiv:2512.22471 / 2607.19379) already show exact-posterior measurement at 10⁻³–10⁻⁴ bit precision. Data-processing monotonicity is the standard expectation.

support.problems:
The headline numbers reproduce exactly. I recomputed measure (b) with scripts/c1_heldout_score.py's score() in memory on docs/c1-sync-sweep-F1-heldout-2026-08-23.json and on the baseline docs/c1-sync-sweep-corrected-2026-08-21.json. At δ_sync = 0.01, T_ep = 16: ε=½ gives r1..r4 = 12/10/10/10, and ε=1 gives 12/12/12/12. The baseline T_ep = 14 gives 12/10/10/10 at both ε. Max r3→r4 is 0.00659 at ε=1, L=2. E1 was enacted (B4′, d4-budget-freeze-v0.1.md), and the 1,315,454-path count is in held-out-laws-proposal §2. I found no later retraction. m1-exit-evidence-map-2026-09-01 (rows 4.3 and 82, line 130) repeats the result as exploratory with the mechanism unassigned. There are four problems.

(1) Boundary-value house rule: the "r2→r3 collapse horizon rose from 8 to 10" is measured against a baseline knife-edge. At (14,8,2) ε=1, the r2→r3 max gap is 0.009985, just 1.5e-5 under δ. It is already flagged as knife-edge in c1-sync-sweep-v0.1.md:158, sweep-rerun-comparison-2026-08-21.md:47 and part2-threshold-freeze-proposal. §8 and the finding do not carry that flag. The T_ep=16 side holds with margin (0.0246 at L=8, 0.0058 at L=10). But if δ were even slightly smaller, the baseline would also be 10, and the finding would read "no change". So the claimed rise depends on the knife-edge.

(2) The finding does not say which ε the collapse rise is at. It happens only at ε=1. At ε=½, r2→r3 collapses at L=8 under both T_ep (gaps 0.0069 and 0.0034).

(3) "Horizon-stable / world property" holds under measure (b) only. Under measure (a), the co-reported law-mass measure, the ε=½ pack moved from 8 to 10 between T_ep 14 and 16. At T_ep 16, all rungs are at 10 at both ε, so measure (a) shows no rung separation anywhere. Measure (b) also rescales by T/(T−L), which changes with T_ep (2.67 at T16 L10 vs 3.5 at T14 L10). So "unchanged L*" compares numbers produced by different scalings. The lesson "sync horizons at ε=½ behave like world properties" therefore claims more than the evidence supports.

(4) "Rung separation vanishes" is true only at the 2-tick L-bucket grain. At ε=1, L=10, r1's scaled worst query is 0.0256 against about 0.017 for r2–r4, so r1 is still worse. Both are above δ, and all are below δ at L=12. The ordering survives; only the bucket separation disappears.

The "teaches" line also says the r1 advantage is horizon-dependent. With only two T_ep points, one of them resting on a knife-edge cell for the collapse sub-claim, that is a single observation, not an established pattern.

novelty.reason: This is a robustness check on the instrument's own exact ceilings: integer synchronization horizons L* at a single threshold δ_sync = 0.01, for one world family (16, L even, 2), rerun at T_ep = 16 after an erratum. It involves no learner, and it shows no general phenomenon an ML or interpretability reader could take away. The ε = ½ half says a world quantity did not change when the episode got longer. That is the expected null, and it matters only because paper 1 needs its ceilings to be horizon-stable. The ε = 1 half, where the r2–r4 pack rises to r1's 12 and rung separation "vanishes", is a coarse integer tie at a single δ, so it lands exactly on a boundary. The house rule says to recheck that at the finest grain, and the note does not: the δ and TV sweeps at T_ep = 16 are unrun and no mechanism is assigned. Both the note and its v0.1.1 corrections label it exploratory. What it teaches is that rung separation under measure (b) is sensitive to T_ep at ε = 1. That is a caveat the paper must report so its interface-ladder claims are not over-read, not a finding. It belongs in a robustness or limitations appendix. Nothing in the prior art is contradicted or extended. Shai et al. and the Bayesian wind-tunnel papers already make exact-ceiling worlds routine, and a filter's synchronization time depending on the horizon and on the noise parameter is what the standard view of filtering predicts.
novelty.nearest_prior: Exact-posterior synchronization and the transient length of mixed-state or causal-state filters, from computational mechanics (Shalizi & Crutchfield, cond-mat/9907176; the synchronization literature following Crutchfield) and as used in the Bayesian wind tunnels (arXiv:2512.22471). The project-internal predecessor is the T_ep = 14 horizon table in docs/held-out-confirmation-v0.1.md §2.

findings.claim: Per-cell max adjacent-rung statutory gaps at L ∈ {2,4} are bimodal. r3→r4 ranges 0.000043–0.003728. r1→r2 and r2→r3 range 0.049943–0.184571, and no cell max lies in (0.003728, 0.049943). Individual query gaps form a continuum with no empty decade (698 entries).
